title: Evaluator: _resolve_validity_chains infinite-loops on conflicting ivsameValidityAs chains
description:
CONFIRMED HANG (reproduced; 8s timeout killed process, exit 124).

src/handler/evaluator.py:_resolve_validity_chains() runs a fixed-point loop:
    while changed:
        for x, y in g.subject_objects(iv:ivsameValidityAs):
            b = g.value(y, iv:ivisValid)
            if existing != b: g.set((x, iv:ivisValid, b)); changed=True

If a node X is linked to two contexts with CONFLICTING validity, e.g.:
    ex:A iv:ivsameValidityAs ex:B .   # B ivisValid true
    ex:A iv:ivsameValidityAs ex:C .   # C ivisValid false
then g.set replaces A's value each pass: true -> false -> true -> ... forever.

Impact: expressionValue is untrusted user input parsed verbatim into the eval
graph. A crafted (or accidental) expression hangs evaluate_intent() in the
background dispatch task with no timeout, pinning a CPU core indefinitely (DoS).

Fix options:
- Detect conflict: if a node already has ivisValid set to a different value this
  pass, stop and treat the node as invalid (or log a conflict condition).
- Or compute via union-find / single forward pass and only propagate when the
  target value is consistent; bound iterations to len(nodes) and bail with a
  logged warning if exceeded.
Add a regression test with the conflicting-chain Turtle above asserting it
returns (does not hang).
acceptance_criteria: Conflicting ivsameValidityAs chains terminate without hanging; regression test added; existing validity tests still pass.

title: Handler: PATCH adding an expression to an intent without one never writes tmf:hasExpression link
description: IntentRepository.update() (src/graph/repositories/intent_repository.py:289-318) builds INSERT lines for the expression node (<expr_uri> rdf:type/expressionIri/expressionValue) but never re-inserts the <intent> tmf:hasExpression <expr_uri> link. When the intent ALREADY had an expression the link survives (deterministic _expr_uri), so existing tests pass. But when an intent was created with no expression and a PATCH adds one, the link is missing: the expression triples become orphaned and get_by_id()'s 'OPTIONAL { <uri> tmf:hasExpression ?exprUri ... }' block never matches, so the expression is invisible to the API AND never evaluated by the handler (evaluate_intent queries tmf:hasExpression). Fix: always emit '<uri> tmf:hasExpression <expr_uri> .' in the INSERT when expression is patched. Add a regression test for create-without-expr then PATCH-add-expr → expression visible + evaluated.

title: Implement DeliveryExpectation and PropertyExpectation evaluation (tio_core + tmf_icm_eval)

None of these are evaluated in Python. Intents using DeliveryExpectation or PropertyExpectation types will silently pass instead of checking delivery membership or boolean property values.

title: Implement validity window evaluation (tmf_validity_eval.rules) in evaluator.py

An intent expression that gates on iv:ivvalidIf or iv:ivisValid will silently pass regardless of whether the temporal validity window is open. This means time-bounded intents are never degraded when out-of-window.
acceptance_criteria: evaluate_turtle_conditions() resolves iv:ivisValid and iv:ivvalidIf chains; expressions using validity conditions pass/fail correctly; unit tests cover valid and expired window cases

title: Implement set_ops evaluation in evaluator.py (setIsMember, setIntersectsWith, setForAll, etc.)

title: Fix Fuseki inference: GenericRuleReasoner does not fire via SPARQL in Fuseki 5.x
description: Fuseki 5.x SPARQL execution operates at the DatasetGraph level, bypassing the ja:InfModel wrapper. Data is stored correctly in tmf921-eval but no inferred triples appear in SPARQL results — not even simple monotonic rules like tioProbeIsIntent. Options: (1) reconfigure eval dataset so Fuseki routes SPARQL through the InfModel (different assembler pattern or dataset type), (2) move quantity comparison evaluation to the Python application layer in evaluator.py — parse expression with RDFLib, apply ge/lt checks directly. Currently tracked by 7 xfail tests in tests/integration/test_hsi_eval_conditions.py. All in-range condition tests xfail; all out-of-range tests pass correctly.
close_reason: Moved quantity condition evaluation to Python/RDFLib in evaluator.py. Covers quanatLeast, quanatMost, quangreater, quansmaller, quanexactly, quaninRange. 44 new tests all pass (was 7 xfail). Full suite: 351 passed, 97.16% coverage.

title: SPARQL injection via unvalidated resource IDs in URI position
description:
Path-parameter resource IDs (intent_id, spec_id, report_id, hub_id) flow unvalidated into SPARQL URI positions (<...>) across all GET/PATCH/DELETE endpoints. src/graph/nodes.py builds URIs by raw f-string interpolation (e.g. intent_graph_uri: f'{_BASE}/intents/{intent_id}'), and repositories embed these as <{uri}> in queries. _esc() only escapes double-quoted literal context, not the <> URI context, and is not even applied to IDs.

ATTACK: A client sends DELETE /tmf-api/intentManagement/v5/intent/x%3E%20%7B%7D%20%7D%3B%20DROP%20ALL%3B%20... — Starlette URL-decodes the path param so intent_id contains '> } }; DROP ALL; ...'. The '>' terminates the SPARQL URI and the remainder is injected. DELETE/PATCH use client.update() (SPARQL UPDATE), so a single crafted request can execute DROP ALL or arbitrary INSERT/DELETE — full data destruction. GET endpoints (query()) are read-only but still leak/abuse.

Create paths use server-generated uuid4 (safe), but every read/update/delete path takes the ID from the URL.

FIX: Validate every path-param ID against a strict pattern (e.g. uuid4 regex, or ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$) at the router boundary before it reaches nodes.py — reject with 404/400 otherwise. Optionally also percent-encode IDs when building URIs. Affected: src/api/routers/{intent,intent_spec,intent_report,hub}.py, src/graph/nodes.py, all repositories.
acceptance_criteria: All path-param IDs validated/sanitised before SPARQL interpolation; injection attempt returns 4xx and cannot alter the store; regression test with a malicious ID on GET/PATCH/DELETE.

title: FusekiClient: no retry/backoff for transient HTTP failures
description:
src/graph/store.py issues every SPARQL query/update/GSP call as a single httpx
attempt with raise_for_status() and no retry. Fuseki is the sole persistence layer,
so any transient connection reset, DNS blip, or 5xx fails the whole API request (or
silently drops a background eval/notification).

Recommend:
- Add bounded retry with exponential backoff + jitter for idempotent operations
  (SELECT/ASK/GSP GET/GSP PUT, ensure_dataset) on httpx.TransportError and 502/503/504.
  Be conservative with non-idempotent SPARQL UPDATE (INSERT DATA is not safely
  retryable in general) — only retry on connect errors where no request was sent.
- Configure httpx limits/keepalive and a connect timeout distinct from read timeout
  (currently a single 30s timeout for everything).
- Consider a lightweight circuit breaker so a Fuseki outage fails fast rather than
  piling up 30s-timeout requests.

Note: health() already swallows httpx.HTTPError, and get_observations_turtle()
handles 404 — but the core query/update/gsp_* paths have no resilience.
acceptance_criteria: Idempotent Fuseki calls retry transient failures with backoff; timeouts split connect/read; behaviour covered by tests using respx to simulate transient 503/connect errors.

title: Handler: no timeout or size bound around untrusted-Turtle evaluation (DoS)
description:
evaluate_turtle_conditions() parses and runs unbounded graph algorithms over
expressionValue, which is untrusted user input. dispatch_evaluation() (src/handler/
dispatcher.py) awaits evaluate_intent() with NO timeout, in a fire-and-forget task.

Amplifiers:
- set:setforAll clones the entire graph once per container member
  (O(members x |graph|) memory/CPU; see evaluator.py:_eval_for_all). A large
  container + large graph is a memory/CPU bomb.
- Combined with the _resolve_validity_chains hang (BBF_921-5r0), a single crafted
  expression can wedge a worker indefinitely.

Recommend:
- Wrap evaluate_intent (or evaluate_turtle_conditions) in asyncio.wait_for /
  a thread executor with a configurable timeout; on timeout return Degraded with
  reason='evaluation timeout' and log.
- Bound input size: reject/short-circuit expressionValue above a configurable byte
  limit and/or triple-count after parse, returning Degraded.
- Consider running the synchronous evaluator in a thread/process pool so a runaway
  evaluation cannot block the event loop (it is CPU-bound and currently runs inline
  on the loop).

Links: [[5r0]].
acceptance_criteria: Evaluation is bounded by a configurable timeout and input-size limit; runaway/oversized expressions return Degraded with a clear reason instead of hanging; tests cover timeout and oversize paths.

title: Evaluator: top-level log:match family ignored without an enclosing combinator
description:
CONFIRMED (reproduced). A satisfiable bare log:match returns Degraded:
  input: ex:iface ex:state ex:Up . ex:cond log:match ( ex:iface ex:state ex:Up ) .
  result: Degraded, reason='No quantity conditions found in expression', conditions=[]

Root cause: log:match / log:matchAll / log:matchAny / log:matchNone / log:matchOne
/ log:matchStatement are dispatched by PROPERTY in _eval_node, but:
- _find_evaluation_roots() only recognises log:allOf/anyOf/noneOf/oneOf as roots,
  so a bare log:match expression yields no roots and falls through to flat-scan.
- _flat_scan() dispatches only by rdf:type and has no entry for the log:* match
  predicates, so the node is never evaluated.
Net effect: any expression whose top level is a log:match-family check (not wrapped
in a logical combinator) is silently skipped and the intent is reported Degraded
regardless of whether the triple actually holds.

Every existing test wraps log:match in log:allOf (tests/unit/test_logical_operators.py),
which is why this was missed.

Fix: in flat_scan (or a dedicated root finder), also detect nodes carrying a
log:match/matchAll/matchAny/matchNone/matchOne/matchStatement predicate and route
them through _eval_node. Add tests for each bare match operator (pass + fail).
acceptance_criteria: Bare top-level log:match/matchAll/matchAny/matchNone/matchOne/matchStatement are evaluated correctly; tests added for pass and fail per operator.

title: Implement ig:GuaranteeReportingExpectation evaluator support
description: ig:GuaranteeReportingExpectation is a subclass of icm:ReportingExpectation that configures guarantee-period reporting. Like icm:ObservationReportingExpectation and iv:ValidityReportingExpectation, handler should check icm:result "true"^^xsd:boolean on the node, defaulting to Degraded when absent. Dispatch in _eval_node, add to _flat_scan, and add to _SIMPLE_FAIL_TYPES.

title: Implement iv:ValidityReportingExpectation evaluator support
description: iv:ValidityReportingExpectation is a subclass of icm:ReportingExpectation that requests intent reports explicitly stating validity of intent elements. Like icm:ObservationReportingExpectation, it is a reporting configuration rather than a constraint. Handler should check icm:result "true"^^xsd:boolean on the node (set by dispatcher when a report is generated), defaulting to Degraded when absent. Dispatch in _eval_node, add to _flat_scan, and add to _SIMPLE_FAIL_TYPES.

title: Implement insp:valueSelectedFor evaluator support
description: The ontology defines insp:valueSelectedFor as a boolean leaf: true if for the intent element (rdf:first) and ObjectTemplate (rdf:rest/rdf:first), the values from the remaining container args were selected. Extends the existing insp:inspvalueSelected handler by scoping it to a specific intent element + ObjectTemplate pair. Dispatch in _eval_node and add to _flat_scan.

title: Implement insp:chosenAnyFor evaluator support
description: The ontology defines insp:chosenAnyFor as a boolean leaf: true if for the intent element given as rdf:first, any of the ContentTemplate args (rdf:rest list) was chosen. Mirrors insp:chosenAllFor but with any-semantics (OR instead of AND). Dispatch in _eval_node and add to _flat_scan.

title: Implement insp:chosenAllFor evaluator support
description: The ontology defines insp:chosenAllFor as a boolean leaf: true if for the intent element given as rdf:first, all ContentTemplate args (rdf:rest list) were chosen. Requires extracting the intent element as the first arg and iterating remaining args as templates. Dispatch in _eval_node and add to _flat_scan.

title: Implement insp:chosenAll evaluator support
description: The ontology defines insp:chosenAll as a boolean leaf condition: true if all insp:ContentTemplate instances listed as args (rdf:list off the function node) were chosen. The evaluator has no handler. Semantics: for each ContentTemplate arg, check that insp:chosenHandlingDomain or equivalent "chosen" assertion is present in the graph. Dispatch in _eval_node and add to _flat_scan.

title: Implement icm:ObservationReportingExpectation evaluator support
description: The ICM ontology defines icm:ObservationReportingExpectation as an expectation type alongside DeliveryExpectation and PropertyExpectation, but the evaluator has no handler for it. Need to clarify the pass/fail semantics from the ontology (likely passes if an observation report of the expected type has been received within the validity window) and add a _eval_observation_reporting_expectation handler in _eval_node.

title: Implement set: graph-traversal set builders (resourcesOfType, resourcesWithProperty, resourcesWithPropertyObject, typesOfMembers, valuesOfObjectProperty)
description: These are set constructors that query the graph to build containers dynamically: set:resourcesOfType — resources matching a given rdf:type; set:resourcesWithProperty — resources that have a given property; set:resourcesWithPropertyObject — resources where property=object; set:typesOfMembers — the rdf:types of all container members; set:valuesOfObjectProperty — values of a property across container members. All produce derived containers consumed by downstream operators. Requires SPARQL-style graph traversal within _eval_node.

title: Implement set: temporal extrema (newestMember, oldestMember)
description: set:newestMember and set:oldestMember return the single member of a container that has the most recent or earliest timestamp (likely via a timestamp property or ivi:isValidIn validity window). Returns a single-member container or the resource itself. Useful for 'most recent observation' patterns without going through met:metlastvalue.

title: Implement set: temporal filter operators (membersAfter, membersBefore, membersSameTime, membersWhile)
description: set:membersAfter, set:membersBefore, set:membersSameTime, set:membersWhile — each takes a container and a time/validity argument and returns a derived container filtered by temporal membership. Used as set constructors that produce a container for downstream operators. Requires understanding of how time/validity is expressed on rdfs:member resources in the graph (likely via ivi:isValidIn or timestamp literals).

title: Implement set: membership/emptiness tests (elementOf, empty)
description: set:elementOf — boolean: rdf:first resource is a direct rdfs:member of every container in the remaining args. set:empty — boolean: every container arg has zero rdfs:members. Both are leaf boolean conditions (like set:setisMember) that return pass/fail and should be dispatched in _eval_node and added to _flat_scan.

title: Implement set: basic algebra operators (union, intersection, difference)
description: The ontology defines set:union, set:intersection, set:difference as set constructors that take two or more rdfs:Container arguments and return a derived container of rdfs:members. These are used as intermediate value nodes (producing a container) that other operators (e.g. set:setisMember, set:setforAll) can then consume. Need _eval_node to materialise the result container as a new blank node with rdfs:member triples so downstream operators see it as a plain container.

title: Implement quan: set-aggregation functions (sumOfSet, multiplicationOfSet, meanOfSet, medianOfSet, greatestInSet, smallestInSet)
description: The ontology defines set-based aggregation variants of the arithmetic functions. Each takes one or more rdfs:Container arguments and aggregates across their rdfs:member elements of type quan:Quantity. Produces a computed rdf:value. Requires _compute_math_functions to enumerate container members, collect their rdf:value literals, and materialise the aggregation result on the function node.

title: Implement quan: n-ary aggregation functions (mean, median, greatest, smallest)
description: The ontology defines quan:mean, quan:median, quan:greatest, quan:smallest as functions over an n-arg RDF list of quan:Quantity nodes. They produce a computed quan:Quantity output (rdf:value). Like binary arithmetic, these are intermediate value nodes. Need a computation pass that walks the rdf:list, collects rdf:value literals from each arg, applies the aggregation, and materialises the result as rdf:value on the function node.

title: Implement quan: binary arithmetic functions (sum, difference, division, multiplication)
description: The ontology defines quan:sum, quan:difference, quan:division, quan:multiplication as functions that take two quan:Quantity arguments and produce a computed quan:Quantity output (rdf:value). These are intermediate value nodes used as inputs to comparator conditions, not boolean conditions themselves. Need to add a computation pass in _compute_math_functions (similar to mf:mfpoly) that materialises rdf:value on these nodes so downstream comparators can fire.

title: Implement quan: short-name aliases (atLeast, atMost, greater, smaller, exactly, inRange)
description: The ontology defines short-name comparator classes (quan:atLeast, quan:atMost, quan:greater, quan:smaller, quan:exactly, quan:inRange) as distinct URIs from the currently-handled quan:quanatLeast etc. variants. The evaluator only dispatches on the quanat-prefixed forms. Need to either add the short-name URIs to _TWO_ARG_OPS and _eval_range, or confirm they are aliases and map them.

title: Notifications: event payload nests resource under 'event' instead of TMF '{resourceName}' key
description: src/services/notification_service.py:_build_payload() emits the envelope with 'event': resource — the resource dict placed directly under 'event'. The OAS-generated payload models (e.g. src/api/schemas/models/intent_create_event_payload.py: IntentCreateEventPayload has a single field 'intent') show TMF921 requires the resource nested one level deeper: {... 'event': { 'intent': <resource> }}. Same applies to intentReport/intentSpecification events. As written, a hub consumer validating against the TMF921 OAS event schema will reject every notification. Fix: map EventType → payload key (intent / intentReport / intentSpecification) and wrap as 'event': { <key>: resource }. Update tests/integration/test_notifications.py envelope assertions accordingly.

title: Evaluator: latest-observation selection uses lexicographic string compare on timestamps
description: src/handler/evaluator.py:_latest_observation_value() (lines 289-306) picks the most recent met:Observation via 'str(obtained_at) > best_time' — a lexicographic string comparison. This is only correct when every obtainedAt literal shares an identical ISO-8601 format and timezone. CLAUDE.md documents that RDFLib normalises an xsd:dateTime 'Z' suffix to '+00:00' on round-trip, while observation_store.build_observation_turtle() writes the 'Z' form. A graph that mixes freshly-written ('...Z') and round-tripped ('...+00:00') observations will sort incorrectly ('+' (0x2B) < 'Z' (0x5A) < digits), so the handler can resolve a STALE observation and evaluate against an outdated metric value. Fix: parse obtained_at to a timezone-aware datetime (e.g. datetime.fromisoformat after normalising Z) and compare as datetimes; fall back to string compare only on parse failure.

title: Evaluator silently returns Fulfilled with zero conditions when a combinator wraps only unknown operators
description: src/handler/evaluator.py:_eval_node() returns (True, []) for any node it does not recognise (line 977, 'Unknown/opaque — pass silently'). This is intended for non-evaluable elements (icm:Context, icm:Target). But combined with the tree path in evaluate_turtle_conditions: if a log:allOf/anyOf root wraps ONLY nodes whose operator type is unsupported/misspelled, every child returns True with no conditions, the combinator passes, overall_passed=all([True])=True, and the intent is reported Fulfilled with an empty conditions list — a silent false positive that hides a malformed or unsupported TIO expression. The flat-scan path guards against this ('No quantity conditions found' → Degraded) but the tree path does not. Fix: distinguish 'evaluated True' from 'nothing evaluable' (e.g. return an Optional[bool]/sentinel, or count leaf evaluations) and treat a root that produced zero real leaf evaluations as Degraded with reason 'no evaluable conditions'.

title: Implement intent specification template conformance evaluation (tmf_insp_eval.rules)
description: tmf_insp_eval.rules covers spec-validation expressions: inspValueSelected (checks chosen value is in allowed set), inspChosenAny (any content template has content), inspUsedVocabularyFor (intent uses terms from vocabulary). None are evaluated in Python. Intents that declare conformance to an IntentSpecification template cannot be validated against that template's constraints.
acceptance_criteria: evaluate_turtle_conditions() evaluates insp:inspvalueSelected, insp:inspchosenAny, insp:inspusedVocabularyFor nodes; unit tests cover valid selection, invalid selection, and empty vocabulary cases

title: Implement Guarantee report state derivation (tmf_guarantee_eval.rules)
description: tmf_guarantee_eval.rules maps ig:igGuaranteeAccepted/Rejected events onto ig:igstate on guarantee reports (igReportStateCompliant, igReportStateDegraded). Without this, IntentReport nodes for guarantee-type intents never get a state value, so guarantee reports are always structurally incomplete. Requires Python to walk the event/report graph and write igstate triples or to expose this via the handlerState graph.
acceptance_criteria: Guarantee-type intent evaluation writes correct ig:igstate to the guarantee report node; integration test covers both compliant and degraded guarantee scenarios

title: Evaluation graph keyed per-intent causes concurrent-eval race condition
description:
src/handler/evaluator.py uses eval_graph_uri(intent_id) (src/graph/nodes.py:32) — a temporary named graph keyed solely by intent_id. evaluate_intent does: gsp_post(eval_graph, turtle) [additive merge] → query state → DROP SILENT GRAPH <eval_graph> in a finally block.

Evaluations are scheduled on every intent create AND every update (intent_service schedules schedule_evaluation each time). Two evaluations of the SAME intent overlapping in time (e.g. rapid create-then-PATCH, or PATCH burst) share the same eval graph URI. Consequences:
  - gsp_post is POST (merge), so concurrent loads pile triples from both runs into one graph → wrong inferred handlingState.
  - One task's finally DROP can delete the other task's data mid-query → the second eval sees an empty graph and defaults to Degraded.

FIX: Make the eval graph unique per evaluation, not per intent — append a uuid4 to eval_graph_uri (e.g. eval/{intent_id}/{run_id}). Each run loads, queries, and drops its own isolated graph. Update evaluator.evaluate_intent and nodes.eval_graph_uri signature accordingly.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent evaluations of the same intent use isolated eval graphs; no cross-contamination of triples or premature DROP; handlingState is deterministic per run.

title: Fire-and-forget notification/evaluation tasks may be GC'd before completion
description:
NotificationService.schedule() (src/services/notification_service.py:83) and schedule_evaluation() (src/handler/dispatcher.py:79) both call asyncio.create_task() and return the Task, but every caller discards the return value (intent_service.create/update/delete, intent_spec_service, intent_report_service, dispatch_evaluation).

The asyncio event loop keeps only a WEAK reference to bare tasks. A task with no strong reference held anywhere can be garbage-collected mid-execution and silently cancelled (documented asyncio footgun, see asyncio.create_task docs). This is more likely under load / many concurrent requests. Result: notifications to hub subscribers and intent evaluations (IntentReport creation) may be randomly dropped with no error.

The bound-method coroutine keeps the service instance alive, but NOT the task object itself, so the risk stands even though services are created per-request.

FIX: Retain strong references — keep a module-level/app-level set of pending tasks, add each created task to it, and attach task.add_done_callback(set.discard). Apply in notification_service.schedule and dispatcher.schedule_evaluation.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduled background tasks are guaranteed to run to completion (held in a tracked set with done-callback cleanup); no task GC drop under concurrent load.

title: Translate dlog rules to Apache Jena format + write docs/12

A design doc docs/12 - load_dlog.md is required covering: dlog vs Jena syntax differences, translation decisions, known limitations (FORALL, NAF), file inventory, and how to load in Fuseki via assembler. Deliverables: docs/12 - load_dlog.md, 13 .rules files in ontology/jena-rules/, one master tio_all.rules concatenating all rules.
close_reason: 13 Jena rule files written to ontology/jena-rules/, docs/12 - load_dlog.md created. All 291 tests still passing at 98.38% coverage.

title: Fix test_generated_models.py: 6 LifecycleStatus failures (NameError + missing can_transition_to)
description: TestLifecycleStateMachine uses LifecycleStatus.ACKNOWLEDGED, LifecycleStatus.ACTIVE etc. and calls .can_transition_to() on them. Two problems: (1) LifecycleStatus is not imported (same commented-out import as the fixture bug), and (2) can_transition_to() does not exist on the generated Pydantic model — the FSM lives in src/services/state_machine.py as validate_transition(from, to). Fix: either (a) add a LifecycleStatus enum with can_transition_to() to the patched generated models via scripts/patch_generated_models.py, or (b) rewrite TestLifecycleStateMachine to call state_machine.validate_transition() directly, which is the actual implementation being tested.
close_reason: Fixed: 25 fixture errors resolved via standalone test models in tests/unit/conftest.py; 6 FSM failures resolved by rewriting TestLifecycleStateMachine to use validate_transition(). All 31 tests now pass (322 total, 98.38% coverage).

title: Fix test_generated_models.py: 25 fixture errors (Intent, IntentPatch not found)
description: tests/unit/test_generated_models.py has its import block commented out. Classes like Intent, IntentPatch, JsonLdExpression, TurtleExpression are used as pytest fixture parameters (e.g. def test_missing_name_raises(self, Intent)) but no fixtures with those names are defined anywhere. pytest fails at setup with 'fixture Intent not found' for all 25 affected tests. Fix: add a conftest.py in tests/unit/ that imports these classes from src.api.schemas.generated and exposes them as fixtures, or uncomment and correct the import in test_generated_models.py and convert the test methods to not use fixture injection for plain class references.
close_reason: Fixed: 25 fixture errors resolved via standalone test models in tests/unit/conftest.py; 6 FSM failures resolved by rewriting TestLifecycleStateMachine to use validate_transition(). All 31 tests now pass (322 total, 98.38% coverage).

title: Evaluator: _eval_node performs ~30 sequential rdf:type membership tests per node
description:
_eval_node (evaluator.py) dispatches by running up to ~30 separate
(node, RDF.type, X) in g membership checks in sequence (quan two-arg x10, inRange,
6 set ops, ICM/IG/IV expectation types, 7 INSP functions, etc.) plus the _TWO_ARG_OPS
loop. For a tree of N nodes this is ~30N graph lookups; flat_scan likewise iterates
~30 rdf:types calling g.subjects each.

Optimisation: fetch the node's types once -- types = set(g.objects(node, RDF.type))
-- and dispatch via a precomputed {type_uri: handler} dict. Same for the two-arg/
inRange comparators. Reduces per-node dispatch from O(operators) to O(1) plus the
single type fetch.

Low risk, mechanical; mainly benefits large expression trees. Keep _SIMPLE_FAIL_TYPES
and flat_scan registration in sync (per CLAUDE.md evaluator gotcha).
acceptance_criteria: Dispatch reads node types once and routes via a dict; all evaluator tests pass unchanged; no behavioural change.

title: Evaluator/observations: O(metrics x observations) metric resolution + unbounded observation graph growth
description:
Two compounding scaling problems on the hot evaluation path:

1. _latest_observation_value(g, metric) (evaluator.py) scans ALL met:Observation
   subjects in the graph for every metric it resolves. _resolve_metric_refs calls
   it once per metlastValue node and once per distinct quantity-condition operand,
   so cost is O(conditions x observations).
   Fix: build a single index in one pass over met:Observation nodes:
   metric -> (latest_dt, value), then resolve each reference in O(1).

2. write_observation() (src/handler/observation_store.py) GSP-POST-appends a new
   met:Observation to the per-intent observations graph on every reading and never
   prunes. The graph grows without bound; get_observations_turtle() ships the whole
   graph into the eval graph each cycle, so evaluation cost grows linearly with the
   total number of historical observations for the intent.
   Fix: keep only the latest-N (or latest per metric) observations, or prune by age;
   alternatively resolve latest values via a SPARQL query with ORDER BY/LIMIT instead
   of materialising the full history into rdflib.

Benefit: keeps per-evaluation cost bounded as an intent accumulates telemetry.
acceptance_criteria: Metric resolution uses a single-pass index (no per-metric full scan); observation graph growth is bounded (pruning or query-based latest-value); benchmark/test demonstrates flat eval cost as observation count grows.

title: Lint: ruff reports 39 errors; CLAUDE.md mandates ruff-clean src/
description: '.venv/bin/ruff check src/' reports 39 errors. Breakdown: 17x F821 undefined-name (forward refs in generated pydantic models under src/api/schemas/models — exclude via per-file-ignores rather than editing generated code), 12x E402 module-import-not-at-top (the '_background_tasks: set = set()' definition was placed BEFORE the imports in src/handler/dispatcher.py:13 and src/services/notification_service.py:15 — move it below the import block), 7x F541 f-string-without-placeholders (src/graph/repositories/intent_repository.py:312-317,330 — the expression-update WHERE block uses f-prefixed plain strings; drop the f), 2x E741 ambiguous 'l' (evaluator.py:219,245 math-fn coefficient — rename to 'scale' or 'lead'), 1x F841 unused var. Goal: 'ruff check src/' exits clean per CLAUDE.md Rules. Mostly auto-fixable; F821 needs a pyproject per-file-ignore for schemas/models/*.

title: Cleanup: IntentService.create has dead no-op loop overwriting payload fields with themselves
description: src/services/intent_service.py:73-76 — 'for f in ("id","href","creationDate","lastUpdate"): if f in data: payload[f] = payload[f]' assigns each key to itself, a no-op. The intended effect (server values win over caller-supplied values) is already achieved because the payload dict literal places server-set keys AFTER '**data'. Remove the loop and the misleading 'server value wins' comment to avoid implying stripping logic that isn't there.

title: Evaluator/state_writer: Decimal operands downcast to float, losing precision in reports and handlerState
description: Comparisons in evaluator.py correctly use Decimal, but the returned condition dicts downcast to float: _eval_two_arg returns 'observed': float(obs), 'bound': float(bnd) (line 507); _eval_range likewise (line 531). state_writer._condition_block then serialises these floats back as ^^xsd:decimal (lines 104-111). So a metric like 0.1+0.2 or a high-precision SLA bound is written to the handlerState graph and IntentReport with binary-float rounding error, and the OODA Decide-step SPARQL (which reads imo:observedValue/imo:boundValue as xsd:decimal) sees the lossy value. Fix: keep Decimal end-to-end — store str(Decimal) in the condition dict and emit that string in the Turtle. Low blast radius but a correctness/precision issue for quantity intents.

title: Optimisation: set:setforAll rebuilds the entire RDF graph per member (O(members x |graph|))
description: src/handler/evaluator.py:_eval_for_all() calls _substitute_node(g, member_var, member) for every member of the container (line 713). _substitute_node (lines 604-613) copies ALL triples of the graph into a fresh rdflib.Graph each call, so evaluating setforAll over N members on a graph of T triples is O(N*T) allocations. For modest expressions this is fine, but it scales poorly and is the only evaluator path that clones the graph. Optimisation: substitute only within the condition subtree reachable from condition_orig, or evaluate the condition with a variable→member binding map passed down through _eval_node instead of materialising a whole new graph. Behaviour must stay identical; reuse existing test_set_ops coverage.

title: Add type-propagation inference for negotiation-related nodes (tmf_ext_eval.rules)
description: tmf_ext_eval.rules defines type propagation for ut:Utility, pre:Preference, pbi:BestProposalReport, and pbi:Proposal. Currently the Python evaluator has no inference layer so these nodes never acquire their supertype labels. This only matters if SPARQL queries or the ProbeIntent/JudgePreference flows rely on inferred types rather than direct assertions.
acceptance_criteria: ProbeIntent negotiation flow correctly classifies utility and preference nodes; SPARQL queries against the tmf921 dataset return correct rdf:type inferences for ext-ontology resources

title: Implement math function evaluation (tmf_mathfn_eval.rules): logistic, poly, mapping
description: tmf_mathfn_eval.rules marks mf:mflogistic, mf:mfpoly, mf:mfmapping nodes as fun:funFunction subtypes. The rules are type-propagation only — actual function computation (applying the logistic sigmoid, polynomial, or piecewise mapping to an input) is not defined anywhere in the rule files. Python would need to implement the actual math. Currently these nodes silently pass.
acceptance_criteria: evaluate_turtle_conditions() computes output of mf:mflogistic, mf:mfpoly, and mf:mfmapping function nodes; result fed into downstream quantity comparators; unit tests cover each function type

title: /health always reports status UP even when graph store is DOWN
description:
src/main.py:46 health() returns {"status": "UP"} unconditionally and only reports graph: UP/DOWN as a sub-field, always with HTTP 200. A load balancer / orchestrator probing /health for a 200 will treat the app as healthy even when Fuseki is unreachable and every data operation will 500.

Also seed_data/seed_intents.py wait_for_server() only checks status_code == 200, so it proceeds to POST against a DB-less server.

FIX: Return 503 (or status: DOWN) when graph_up is False, so the endpoint reflects true readiness. Consider separating liveness (app up) from readiness (graph reachable).
acceptance_criteria: /health returns non-200 (or status DOWN) when the graph store is unreachable; readiness reflects DB connectivity.

title: seed_intents.py: lifecycleStatus uses wrong casing for IntentSpecification
description: The INTENT_SPEC payload in seed_data/seed_intents.py passes 'lifecycleStatus': 'Active' (title case). The IntentSpecification service create() spreads **data directly into the payload (intent_spec_service.py:40-48) without overriding lifecycleStatus, so 'Active' is stored verbatim. The state machine and ALL_STATES frozenset use ALL-CAPS values only ('ACKNOWLEDGED', 'ACTIVE', etc.) so the stored value is non-conformant and would fail any FSM transition validation. The four Intent payloads are not affected because intent_service.create() always overwrites lifecycleStatus with 'ACKNOWLEDGED' regardless of what the caller supplies.

title: seed_intents.py: expression.iri missing from all 4 intents
description: All four INTENTS in seed_data/seed_intents.py are missing the 'iri' field on their expression objects. The repository (intent_repository.py:110) only writes the expressionIri triple when iri is present, so all seeded intents will have expression.iri=null in the stored graph and in API responses. This violates the TMF921 spec requirement that iri is a mandatory field on all expression types (IntentExpressionFVO.iri: str - required). The repository does not crash or reject the payload, so the seed runs successfully, but every created intent is non-conformant.

title: seed_intents.py: expressionValue pre-JSON-encoded instead of passing dict directly
description: The JsonLdExpression payloads in seed_data/seed_intents.py call json.dumps({...}) on the expressionValue dict before passing it to the API (lines 31-35, 65-70, 82-88). The intent is to send a structured value, but the sent value is a JSON string not a dict. This still round-trips correctly: base_repository._ser_expr_value() stores strings as-is, and _deser_expr_value() calls json.loads() on read-back for JsonLdExpression, so API responses return the correct dict. However, it is not best practice and differs from what the spec expects at the protocol level. The correct approach is to pass the dict directly and let the repository handle serialization.
